ltpgtlt/pgtltpgtltspangtThe proposed Action has been designed to respond to the needs outlined above through multisectoral emergency relief efforts in combination with strengthened community-based protection focused on Mine Action. The proposed target locations are Muse and Kutkai in Northern Shan, in line with priorities set out in the MHF 2023 First Standard Allocation. The exact locations will be determined at the start of the project, and the number of sites will depend on the size of the selected sites, however, Acted will target at least one site in each township. Acted will liaise with relevant Clusters to select specific locations during the initial stages of the project to avoid duplication of efforts. Acted will ensure good collaboration with other actors present in the area, and notably refer beneficiaries targeted under this intervention to complement the assistance.lt/spangtlt/pgt
ltpgtltbrgt Through the proposed intervention, thecritical needs of 5,500 individuals (of which approximately 50% women and girls) will be addressed. In doing so, the proposed Action will reduce the acute vulnerabilities of conflict-affected households in hard-to-reach areas of Northern Shan States. To achieve this, Acted will provide needs-based and gender-focused assistance through blanket distributions including emergency shelter and non-food item (ESNFI) kits - which is expected to benefit 2,600 individuals - and food assistance in-kind or in cash, for approximately 1,895 individuals. Additionally, all 5,500 individuals will have improved access to protection services. The target sites will be selected based on demographics (including percentage of female headed households), displacement status size, and the response modality will be tailored to the needs of selected sites. Through this targeted assistance, basic household needs will be met, and acute vulnerabilities will be reduced as a result. Based on experience, the project proposes to provide the assistance through blanket distributions to mitigate the risk of unintentionally contributing to communal tensions. In parallel, the proposed Action will reinforce protection services through widespread awareness-raising, strengthening community-based protection mechanisms, and dedicated individual services. As the IDP demographics in targeted townships show an even gender disaggregation, Acted will target 50% female and 50% male beneficiaries for the mine risk education. The gender breakdown for the mine victim assistance will be based on needs, however, based on experience, Acted anticipates an even gender breakdown. As such, the Action is aimed at providing timely and integrated life-saving multi-sectoral emergency relief, as well as improving the overall wellbeing of conflict-affected populations through timely and integrated protection assistance.lt/pgt
ltspangtltbrgt As outlined, humanitarian access to Northern Shan is increasingly restricted. Given these uncertainties surrounding access, remote and mobile service delivery and community-based protections mechanisms (which ensure the participation of targeted people) have been prioritised in Acted’s designed approach. As such, Acted will work with two of its established local partners: ltspangtHsaipen, and Never End Tomorrow (NET).lt/spangt Partners will support the distribution of emergency assistance, and provide critical protection services to targeted communities. Moreover, Acted will work together with ltspangtHALO Trustlt/spangt to provide local partners with comprehensive training on Explosive Ordnance Risk Education, First Aid, and Victim Assistance, to further strengthen community-based awareness-raising to avoid and respond to mine incidents. In parallel, partners will be provided with organizational and institutional capacity-building training by Acted to further strengthen a localized approach and future capacity to respond to community needs, as well as improve their accountability to targeted populations.lt/spangt
